---
title: Subscription or API — at what monthly volume did switching pay off for you?
category: general
---
[Plans](https://undominated.ai/plans/) compares ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, Cursor and Google AI plans against API pricing: the published monthly price, the limits **in the vendor's own words**, and the token volume at which per-token becomes cheaper.

The weak link is the second column. Plan limits are usually published as prose — "higher limits", "fair use", "priority access" — which cannot be turned into a token count without inventing one. So the break-even is exact on the API side and, at best, approximate on the plan side.

Real usage data closes that gap better than any vendor page. If you are willing, post:

```
plan · monthly price · approx. tokens/month · hit a limit? (y/n, how often) · switched? (which way)
```

**Questions**

- At what volume did you switch, and in which direction?
- Which vendor's limits are precise enough to compute a break-even, and which are not?
- What would a *measurable* limit disclosure look like — and should the board rank plans by how precisely they state their limits?
